subject: Entry-level pilot: monthly commitment structure and overage options
messages:
From: Lily Chen <lily@brighthealth.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@brighthealth.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Quick question on minimum monthly and pilot options

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week — Tom and I appreciated the focus on latency and the KV-caching examples. Before we pull procurement in, we have two quick questions about your hosted API pricing:

- Do you require a minimum monthly commit for pilot customers, or is there a no-commit starter path?
- If a minimum is required, what does a short pilot (30–90 days) look like from a billing/credit perspective? Any standard uplift or activation credit you provide for evaluation?

Our legal/procurement team will want to understand invoice cadence (monthly vs. prepaid) and any convertibility of pilot spend to longer-term committed credits. We expect ~3M tokens/month in month 1 if the evaluation goes well, scaling after integration.

Can you share a concise set of options (one-paragraph bullets) and the current public rate card or a short summary? If easier, a one-page SOW example + rate card would work.

Appreciate it — aiming to get procurement looped in next week.

Best,
Lily Chen
Product Manager, Bright Health AI
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lily Chen <lily@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@brighthealth.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on minimum monthly and pilot options

Hi Lily — great to hear from you and glad the walkthrough was useful. Short answers up front, then options.

No strict barrier: we do offer a few common paths depending on how committed you want to be during pilot. Below are three pragmatic options we use for hosted API pilots (we'll follow up with a tailored SOW):

1) Self-serve starter (no commit)
   - No minimum monthly spend; pay-as-you-go at public rates.
   - Ideal for quick functional/eval work, but less predictable unit economics.
   - Activation credit available (typically $1k–$5k depending on expected usage) to offset early dev costs.

2) Soft-commit pilot (recommended for performance validation)
   - 90-day pilot with a small monthly commit (typical entry band: $2.5k–$7.5k / month).
   - Commit is billed monthly and convertible to reserved credit if you convert to Dedicated/annual later.
   - Overages billed at a discounted overage rate (example: public rate * 1.05 capped at 15% premium).
   - We can include a one-time activation credit to cover onboarding.

3) Short-term committed trial (for procurement-friendly path)
   - Prepaid 3-month commitment (e.g., $7.5k total) with a 15% committed discount and priority onboarding.
   - Invoices can be prepaid or net-30 depending on procurement needs.

Attached: Redwood_RateCard_Q4_2026.pdf (rate bands + committed discount tiers) — this is our compact reference. Also happy to attach a short SOW template.

Next steps I propose:
- If procurement wants an invoice/PO-friendly view, we can send a 3-month prepaid SOW and a convertible credit option.
- If you prefer the pay-as-you-go model for initial integration, we can grant a $2k activation credit and keep a soft-commit conversion clause in the SOW.

Cc'ing Aditya (sales lead) to weigh in on the conversion incentives and any promotion we can apply.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0119

Subject: Re: Quick question on minimum monthly and pilot options

Thanks Mina — good framing. One thing to consider: for accounts forecasting ~3M tokens/mo during pilot, propose we offer a small convertibility sweetener:

- If Bright Health converts to a 12-month reserved commitment within 60 days of pilot end, we can credit 100% of pilot committed spend toward the first 3 months of the annual commit (up to an agreed cap).

Operational asks:
- Can we confirm that activation credits can be applied against the first invoice automatically? Procurement often needs that in the SOW.
- Also confirm that overage meters are monthly and visible in the console with token-level breakdowns.

Marissa / Karthik: any constraints from finance or product on the above?

-Aditya
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Mina / Aditya,

Thanks for the options. Procurement here — a few practical questions so we can prepare a PO: 

- Preferred invoice cadence for a 3-month prepaid pilot? We prefer a single prepaid invoice for the pilot period.
- Will Redwood accept a PO for a prepaid pilot and provide a single invoice?
- Need clarity on refundable credits vs. prepaid convertibility — can you confirm if unused prepaid amounts are refundable or automatically converted to account credit?
- Please attach a short SOW and indicate whether the activation credit can be shown as a line-item discount on the invoice.

Also attaching a redline template for the MSA — we typically need to confirm data retention and audit log exports.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Bright Health AI

Subject: Re: Entry-level pilot: monthly commitment structure and overage options

Hi team — thanks for the clear questions. Summary of what Redwood can commit to for a clean procurement path: 

Pilot proposal (convertible prepaid) — recommended for procurement-friendly evaluation:
- Length: 3 months prepaid.
- Amount: $7,500 prepaid (example entry-level band aligned with your 3M tokens/mo expectation).
- Discount: 15% on committed dollars versus public pay-as-you-go.
- Activation credit: $2,000 applied as an invoice line-item discount on the prepaid invoice.
- Convertibility: if Bright Health signs a 12-month reserved commitment within 60 days of pilot close, we will convert the prepaid pilot dollars to reserved credit (no refunds); otherwise unused dollars remain as account credit for 12 months.
- Overage: monthly metering; overages billed at the committed overage rate shown on the attached rate card (we cap overage premium at 15%).
- Invoicing: single prepaid invoice for the pilot period (Net-30 available by request).

Attached: BHA_SOW_draft_20261124.docx — short SOW + billing appendix, and Redwood_RateCard_Q4_2026.pdf.

Requesting next steps from Bright Health:
1) Confirm whether you want the invoice prepaid or Net-30.
2) Approve the SOW draft and we will issue a DocuSign package (link included).
3) If OK, procurement to issue PO referencing deal RDW-2026-BHA-003.

I'll loop in Marissa for finance acceptance; cc'd. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call to finalize wording with procurement.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
